items.name: Rowle-geared Whipstaff

items.name: Admiralty-pattern Anchor
items.buys: Weather-holding, and a faster turnaround in port
items.note: An anchor of the improved pattern with a longer shank and curved arms: it bites in any ground and weighs a little more.

items.name: Bower & Sheet Anchors
items.note: A sheet anchor and a best bower carried together: the ship rides out almost any night, at a cost in cargo space.

items.name: Geared Capstan
items.note: A capstan geared so one crew heaves like two: the anchor comes up fast and the yards faster.

items.name: Night Glass & Royal Mast

items.name: Azimuth Compass & Rutter
items.note: An azimuth compass and a written rutter of every coast: the ship knows its bearing and what lies ahead.

items.name: Trimmed Kentledge

items.name: Copper-bolted Sheathing
items.note: Copper sheathing fastened with copper bolts over greenheart, so the iron below does not rot away: the hardest bottom made.

items.name: Diagonal Planking
items.note: A second skin of greenheart laid diagonally over the frames: the hull stops working in a sea and takes far more shot.

items.name: Bentinck Chain Pumps
items.note: Chain pumps of the improved pattern, worked by fewer hands and moving far more water.

items.name: Orlop Stowage

items.name: Lisbon-cast Brass Guns
items.note: Brass guns cast in the Lisbon foundry and proved with slow-match: a little more weight of fire than other brass guns.

items.name: Arsenale Rudder & Helm
items.note: A teak rudder hung on brass pintles in the Venetian Arsenale way: the ship turns a little sharper.

items.name: Genoese Anchor & Cable
items.buys: Weather-holding, and a faster turnaround in port
items.note: A bar-iron anchor on a cable laid from Ligurian hemp as well as Manila: the ship rides easier and swings quicker.

items.name: Antwerp Duck Canvas
items.note: Duck canvas lined with Flemish linen at the seams, as the Antwerp sailmakers cut it: a little more speed from the same wind.

items.name: Elbe Frames
items.note: Live-oak frames with Memel fir ceiling between them, Hamburg fashion: a little more cargo space in the same hull.

items.name: Hanseatic Capstan
items.note: A teak capstan with osmund-iron pawls, as the Lubeck yards fit it: the anchor and yards come up a little faster.

items.name: Danzig Oak Planking
items.note: Doubled planking of the straight Polish oak Gdansk ships, payed with pine pitch: a little stronger than other oak.

items.name: London-pattern Chasers
items.note: Brass chasers bored to the London pattern and proved with English powder: they reach and aim a little further.

items.name: Provencal Jib & Staysail
items.note: A duck jib and staysail dressed with linseed oil, as the Marseille sailmakers do: the ship answers the helm a little quicker.

items.name: Surat Teak Sheathing
items.note: Teak and copper over a bed of coir caulking, as the Surat yards lay it: a little more armour and hull from the same bottom.

items.name: Malabar Chain Pumps
items.note: Teak chain pumps with coco-fibre packing, Kochi fashion: they keep a little more water down.

items.name: Callao Copper-pig Ballast
items.note: Pig-iron ballast topped with copper pigs from the Callao quay: a little stiffer and steadier than plain pig iron.
